header: IN THE LAHORE HIGH COURT, LAHORE
Younas Waqar & another Vs. The State etc.
J U D G M E N T
body: Date of Hearing: 04.11.2026.
Appellants by: Malik Muhammad Azam Awan Advocate.
State by: Ms. Noshe Malik, Deputy Prosecutor General.
Complainant by: Mr. Waqar Hassan Advocate.

MUHAMMAD WAHEED KHAN, J.- Through this appeal, Younas Waqar and Azhar Iqbal (appellants), have challenged their convictions and sentences, awarded to them by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Noorpur Thal, vide judgment dated 28.02.2025, passed in case FIR No.112 dated 28.03.2022, registered under sections 302, 201, 34 PPC, at Police Station Noorpur Thal, District Khushab, whereby, they were convicted and sentenced as under: u/s 302(b) PP C Imprisonment for Life, each for committing Qatl-e-Amd of Zafar Iqbal, deceased with direction to pay compensation of Rs.10-Lacs each, to the legal heirs of the deceased as required under section 544-A Cr.P.C., and in default of payment of compensation amount, to further undergo six months simple imprisonment, each.
u/s 201 PPC Three years simple imprisonment, each and fine of Rs.10,000/- each; in default of payment of fine, to further undergo simple imprisonment for three months, each.
The sentences awarded to both the appellants were directed to run concurrently. Benefit of section 382-B Cr.P.C. was also extended to them.

Crl. Appeal No.28034-J of 2025 2 2. Briefly stated facts of the case as narrated by complainant, Ghous Muhammad (PW.10), in his complaint (Ex.PA), on the basis of which, formal FIR (Ex.PB), was registered, are that on 26.03.2022 at about 3:00 P.M., his brother Zafar Iqbal departed to attend a marriage in the Mohallah but did not return and his cell phone was also switched off; that he alongwith Muhammad Ikramul-Haq and Muhammad Azaad PWs searched for his brother but could not trace him; on 28.03.2022 he moved an application (Ex.PA) to the police station on the basis of which, later on, above-mentioned FIR was lodged. During the course of investigation, complainant moved an application to the SHO concerned by stating therein that during search of his brother Zafar Iqbal on 21.04.2022, Muhammad Waseem Akram informed him that on 26.03.2022, he alongwith Muteh Ullah (PW.12) was going to look after abele (سفیدہ) trees and at 3:20 P.M., when they were coming back and reached near the tubewell of one Saif Ullah Ghabisar, they saw accused persons, Muhammad Azhar, Sami Ullah and Younas Waqar, present there and talking with each other and that at some distance in the field of wheat crop on the unpaved path, Zafar Iqbal and his Bhabhi, Munawar Bibi were also talking with each other; he further told that he alongwith Muteh Ullah (PW.12) witnessed the whole affair and continued their journey towards home; upon this information, the complainant alongwith Muhammad Ikram-ul-Haq went to the house of Muhammad Azhar, accused and inquired about Zafar Iqbal, who firstly refused to divulge anything but on their insistence, the said accused disclosed that deceased Zafar Iqbal was having illicit relations with his sister-in-law Munawar Bibi due to which he was defamed and that Zafar Iqbal had not done fair with them; therefore, the complainant suspected that accused persons, namely, Azhar Iqbal, Younas Waqar, Sami Ullah and Munawar Bibi had abducted his brother Zafar Iqbal and that they should be named in the FIR, hence, these persons were nominated in the FIR as accused and investigation was carried out; on 07.05.2022, during investigation, in the presence of complainant and Muhammad Asif (PW.13), accused/appellant No.1, Younas Waqar made disclosure regarding the murder of Zafar Iqbal and led the police party to the place of occurrence and pointed out the place of murder, in the presence of complainant and PW.13; that dead body was recovered and postmortem examination was conducted on the same day; that Crl. Appeal No.28034-J of 2025 3 on 05.06.2022, in the presence of complainant, as well as, PW.13, Azhar Iqbal, accused/appellant No.2, during police investigation, also made disclosure regarding the murder of Zafar Iqbal and led the police party to the place of occurrence and pointed out the place of murder in presence of the PWs, hence, this case.

3. On culmination of investigation, the appellants were found guilty, hence, report under section 173 Cr.P.C., was submitted to learned trial court, whereby they were summoned to face trial. Charge was framed against the appellants, to which, they pleaded not guilty, hence, trial commenced. In order to prove its case, the prosecution produced, as many as, fifteen witnesses as PWs. Complainant, Ghous Muhammad, appeared as PW.10; Muhammad Waseem and Muteh Ullah, witnesses of last seen, appeared as PW.11 and PW.12, respectively; Muhammad Asif, in whose presence, the appellants made confession of murder of Zafar Iqbal (deceased), appeared as PW.13; Ikram-ul-Haq, in whose and complainant’s presence, PW.11 and PW.12 told that they saw Zafar Iqbal in the company of accused persons, appeared as PW.14; Bashir Ahmad, ASI, who chalked out FIR (Ex.PB), appeared as PW.1, while Ghulam Jilani, 454/MHC-Moharrar, appeared as PW.13; Dr. Khurram Kamran, who conducted autopsy on the dead body of Zafar Iqbal (deceased), appeared as PW.6 and besides other formal witnesses, Muhammad Mushtaq, Sub-Inspector, who conducted investigation in this case, appeared as PW.15. Thereafter, the prosecution closed its evidence by producing certain documentary evidence. After recording the prosecution evidence, appellants were examined under section 342 Cr.P.C., wherein they denied all the allegations leveled against them. They did not opt to record their statements u/s 340(2) Cr.P.C. but produced some documentary evidence in their defence. Learned trial Court after appraising the prosecution evidence convicted and sentenced the appellants, in the above-mentioned terms.

4. In support of the instant appeal, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the appellants contends that the impugned judgment was a result of noncomprehension of real facts and circumstances of the case and it is based upon surmises and conjectures, having no evidentiary foundation; that motive set up by the prosecution has been disbelieved by the learned trial Court; and Crl. Appeal No.28034-J of 2025 4 lastly submits that since, the prosecution has failed to prove its case beyond the “reasonable doubt”, hence, the impugned judgment is not sustainable, therefore, the instant appeal be allowed and the appellants may be acquitted of the charge.

5. On the other hand, by taking exceptions to the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the appellants, learned Deputy Prosecutor General assisted by learned counsel for the complainant has submitted that the prosecution has proved its case ‘beyond shadow of doubt’ against the appellants and successfully established their guilt by producing cogent, trustworthy, reliable, unimpeachable and confidence inspiring evidence in shape of ocular account; the evidence of recovery of weapons of offence and motive and that the investigating officer has declared the appellants to be fully involved in the crime, hence, there is no force in the arguments of learned counsel for the appellants; that the prosecution also remained successful to establish the guilt of the appellants before the learned trial Court, which resulted into their convictions and sentences and finally prayed that this appeal is liable to be dismissed.
6. I have heard learned counsel for the parties, as well as, learned Deputy Prosecutor General for the State and gone through the record with their assistance.

7. Ghous Muhammad son of Sher Muhammad (PW.10), while setting the machinery of law in motion qua the missing of his brother Zafar Iqbal, had reported to the police through Ex.PB (FIR) that his brother Zafar Iqbal had been kidnapped by unknown suspects on account of undisclosed reasons from the area of Mauza Rangpur of District Khushab on 26.03.2022 at about 3:00 P.M. The accused remained unknown till 26.04.2022, whereafter, the complainant made another application (Ex.PM) to the police showing his suspicion against Muhammad Azhar (Azhar Iqbal), Younas Waqar, appellants, Sami Ullah and Munawar Bibi (since acquitted). On going through the contents of Ex.PM, it is found that same was lodged on the information provided by one Muhammad Waseem Akram (PW.11), who apprised the complainant that on 26.03.2022, he alongwith Muteh Ullah (PW.12) had seen Azhar Iqbal, Sami Ullah, Imdad Hussain and Younas Waqar, while standing near the Crl. Appeal No.28034-J of 2025 5 tubewell of one Saif Ullah Ghabisar, at some distance near the wheat crop of one Saif Ullah on a thoroughfare. Zafar Iqbal was talking with his sister-inlaw (بھابھی) Munawar Bibi wife of Saif Ullah, however, they (witnesses) left the place without making any conversation with the deceased or the accused persons. Record manifests that Younas Waqar, appellant was taken into custody by the police on 06.05.2022, who during interrogation confessed his guilt to the effect that he alongwith Sami Ullah and Munawar Bibi caught hold Zafar Iqbal, whereas Azhar Iqbal caused various blows of ‘Chhurri’ on his chest and then cut his throat. Younas Waqar, appellant also identified the place wherein the deceased was allegedly done to death. Thereafter, Younas Waqar also got recovered a decomposed dead body after digging the earth underneath the eucalyptus (سفیدہ) trees, which dead body was later on identified as of Zafar Iqbal through DNA analysis by the Punjab Forensic Science Agency with his brother. Thereafter, Azhar Iqbal was formally arrested in this case, who vide memo Ex.PP dated 05.06.2022, also identified the place of occurrence wherein the deceased was done to death. During investigation, Younas Waqar also got recovered a ‘Kassi’ (P-4) vide recovery memo (Ex.PJ). When the dead body was got recovered, police prepared inquest report (مرگ رپورٹ) and observed the dead body as decomposed and head of deceased was also found cut. Dr. Khurram Kamran (PW.6), conducted autopsy on 07.05.2022 at DHQ Hospital, Jauharabad and on opening of the three cavities i.e. Cranium and spinal cord; thorax and abdomen, all the organs were found decomposed and head was found separated from rest of the body. Femur, a piece of rib, scalp patch with hairs were handed over to police for forensic analysis and after getting Forensic Toxicology Analysis Report (Ex.PAA) drugs were not detected in hairs, in item No.01 and no evidence of poison was detected. After getting DNA and Serologist Analysis Report (Ex.PAB) issued on 02.12.2022, human blood was found on item No.1.1. Calculation of likelihood ratios, two tested individuals, unidentified dead body (item No.2) and Ghous Muhammad (item No.B1) are 483,300 times more likely to be biologically full siblings than unrelated. So based on this report, deceased person whose decomposed dead body was found, was identified as of Zafar Iqbal son of Sher Muhammad, 30 years male sibling of Ghous Muhammad resident of Rangpur, Caste Ghabesar. As per police Crl. Appeal No.28034-J of 2025 6 papers, death occurred approximately 40-days before the day of postmortem. Time between injury and death was immediate within five minutes, time between death and postmortem was about 20-50 days (stage of butyric fermentation).

8. There is no denying that no direct evidence qua the killing of deceased and culpability of appellant, is available in this case and prosecution case primarily structured on the circumstantial evidence in the shape of last seen evidence; extrajudicial confession of Azhar Iqbal made before the complainant Ghaus Muhammad and Muhammad Waseem, PW.10 and PW.11, respectively; and evidence of recovery of dead body of deceased on the disclosure allegedly made by Younas Waqar, appellant No.1. There is hardly any cavil that to award conviction in a case entailing capital punishment, circumstantial evidence could be relied upon but the proof of circumstances in this regard, should be so connected to each other, that it would make a complete chain starting right from the crime scene and the other end reaches to the neck of the accused, without any broken link in it. Having assessed the evidence adduced by the prosecution, keeping in view the above fundamental principle of law, it is observed that while submitting the application (Ex.PA) on 26.04.2022, the complainant Ghous Muhammad, reported to the police that Muhammad Waseem Akram (PW.11) had apprised him on the same day i.e. 26.04.2022 that he (PW.11) alongwith Muteh Ullah (PW.12) had seen Zafar Iqbal (deceased) having conversation with his sister-inlaw (بھابھی), Munawar Bibi (since acquitted) on 21.04.2022, near the tubewell of one Saif Ullah Ghabesar, whereas, other co-accused persons, namely, Azhar Iqbal, Sami Ullah and Younas Waqar were standing at some distance. Muhammad Waseem Akram (PW.11), while deposing before learned trial Court stated that he was a close relative of deceased Zafar Iqbal and factum of missing of Zafar Iqbal (deceased) came to his knowledge on the day of incident i.e. 26.03.2022. Similar was the position of Muteh Ullah (PW.12) who also deposed before learned trial Court that Zafar Iqbal was his close relative and he knew the incident of missing of Zafar Iqbal (deceased) since 26.03.2022 and as per their versions, they had seen the deceased while standing in the company of accused persons on the day of incident i.e. 26.03.2022 but despite having close relations with the complainant, they remained tight lipped till Crl. Appeal No.28034-J of 2025 7 26.04.2022, when after one month of the incident, they first time, disclosed this fact to the complainant, who reported the same to the police on the same day i.e. 26.04.2022 through Ex.PM. So, this piece of evidence i.e. last seen evidence is not worthy of reliance on this score alone. The prosecution had heavily relied upon the factum of recovery of dead body of Zafar Iqbal (deceased) at the instance of Younas Waqar, appellant No.1 on 06.05.2022, who as per prosecution case was done to death by Muhammad Azhar Iqbal, appellant No.2. On in depth analysis of record, it is noticed that he (Azhar Iqbal) alongwith Younas Waqar, appellant No.1, also got ‘Kassi’ (P3) recovered vide recovery memo (Ex.PJ) and identified the place of occurrence through memo (Ex.PP), but no discoveries/recovery memos of the dead body have ever been prepared by the investigating agency. Articles 38 & 39 of Qanun-e-Shahadat Order, 1984 (QSO) enumerate general principle that a confession made to the police or in custody of police could not be proved against the maker. However, Article 40 is the exception to this general rule which says that such information which leads to the discovery of a fact, could be proved against the accused even through he made such disclosure in custody of police. Article 40 of Qanun-e-Shahadat Order, 1984 is reproduced herein for reference: - “How much of information received from accused may be proved.- When any fact is deposed to as discovered in consequence of information received from a person accused of any offence, in the custody of a police officer, so much of such information, whether it amounts to a confession or not, as relates distinctly to the fact thereby discovered, may be proved.”

In a recent verdict rendered by the august Supreme Court of Pakistan in the case of “Zunair Younas and another , outlined the following essential elements to satisfy the procedure of Article 40 of Qanun-e-Shahadat Order, 1984, as under: - (i) Accused must be in lawful police custody in that particular case at the time of making disclosure. A voluntary disclosure made outside custodial context does not attract operation of Article 40 of Qanun-e-Shahadat.

“Zunair Younas and another Vs. The State through P.G. Punjab and another” (PLD 2026 Supreme Court 222) Crl. Appeal No.28034-J of 2025 8 (ii) Information must be specific and must distinctly relate to the fact discovered. Generalized or vague statements are not covered; discovery must be directly traceable to information furnished.
(iii) There must be tangible discovery of a material fact, such as recovery of an object, article, weapon, or place, which was previously unknown to investigating agency.
(iv) There must be clear causal link between disclosure and discovery. The fact must be discovered as direct and immediate consequence of the information provided by accused.

(v) Only that portion of statement which relates distinctly to fact discovered is admissible. Remainder of the statement, including any confessional or incriminating parts not tied to the discovery, remains inadmissible.

(vi) Recovery must be genuine, verifiable, and documented through credible and preferably independent witnesses. Authenticity of discovery is not presumed and must be established through cogent evidence.

(vii) Evidentiary value of discovery must be assessed in conjunction with other corroborative evidence. A discovery alone, even if admissible, is insufficient to sustain conviction unless it fits into an unbroken chain of circumstances.
(bold and underline provided for emphasis)

In another case reported as “Zafar Ali Abbasi and another , it is observed as under: - “In order to bring the case within the ambit of Article 40 of the Qanun-e-Shahadat Order, 1984, the prosecution must prove that a person accused of any offence, in custody of police officer, has conveyed an information or made a statement to the police, leading to discover of new fact concerning the offence, which is not in the prior knowledge of the police. Such information or statement should be in writing and in presence of witnesses. In absence of information or statement from a person, accused of an offence in custody of police officer, discovery of fact alone, would not bring the case of the prosecution under the said Article. According to the prosecution, a dagger used in the commission of the offence was recovered on the disclosure and pointation of the appellant. Surprisingly, the I.O. did not record the information received from the appellant in writing, in presence of a witness, while he was in police custody. The prosecution has failed to establish any disclosure from the appellant, therefore, recovery of the dagger, in the circumstances was immaterial.”
(Under line has been provided for emphasis)

“Zafar Ali Abbasi and another Vs. Zafar Ali Abbasi and others” (2024 SCMR 1773) Crl. Appeal No.28034-J of 2025 9 Likewise, in the case of “Abdul Mateen , the august Supreme Court of Pakistan had held as under: - “The learned High Court had also after scanning the evidence on record came to the conclusion that discovery of dead body on the pointation of respondent was highly doubtful as the prosecution failed to bring on record any memo. about the disclosure of respondent before witnesses or to bring on record any memo. about the seizure of dead body on the pointation of respondent coupled with the fact that memo. was prepared for recovery of blood- stained earth from the place of occurrence but the same has not mentioned about the recovery of dead body of deceased on pointation of respondent accused and the prosecution did not corroborate this piece of evidence through any independent piece of evidence.”

The Hon’ble Division Bench of this Court in the case of “Nadeem Shah , has observed as under: - “In order to prove during trial that the accused actually made a disclosure and subsequently led to the recovery of some fact, it is essential that a memo of his disclosure be prepared. Only the preparation of the memo testified by the witnesses will prove in subsequent trial that the fact was discovered in consequence of a lead and pointing out of the accused.”
(Under line has been provided for emphasis)

In this case, as discussed supra, the prosecution has only brought on record the facts that Younas Waqar, appellant No.1 got recovered ‘Kassi’ used in the crime from the place wherein dead body of deceased was allegedly concealed, whereas Azhar Iqbal, appellant No.2 got recovered the weapon of offence i.e. Chhurri through recovery memos Ex.PJ and Ex.PK, respectively and their unscaled site plans were prepared as Ex.PW and Ex.PX, respectively. Further, both the appellants allegedly identified the place of occurrence wherein the deceased was done to death vide memo Ex.PO and Ex.PP, respectively and the site-plans vide memo Ex.PT and Ex.PU, were also prepared but since no discovery memo of recovery of dead body has ever been prepared by the investigating agency, so this statement of Younas Waqar, appellant No.1, allegedly made to the police, in consequence of that putrefied and mutilated dead body of the deceased, was recovered, under Article 40 of the Qanun-e- Shahadat Order, 1984, also remains unproved as the statement of accused comprising the information regarding the fact in consequence of that dead “Abdul Mateen Vs. Sahib Khan and others” (PLD 2006 Supreme Court 538) “Nadeem Shah Vs. The State” (2024 YLR 1127)

Crl. Appeal No.28034-J of 2025 10 body recovered is relevant fact. On going through the excerpts of the afore referred judgments and Article 40 of the QSO, there should be;- (i) an information or statement from the accused, who must be in lawful police custody in that particular case, (ii) information must be specific and distinctly related to the facts discovered and (iii) it is essential that such disclosure of the accused before the witnesses, a memo of disclosure testified by the witnesses be prepared.

Discovery of fact alone certainly would not bring the case of the prosecution under Article 40 of QSO, in absence of information or statement of accused under police custody and without the same be properly documented (preparation of memo of disclosure through credible witnesses). In that eventuality, the case in hand does not fit in within these parameters.

9. So far as the recovery of bloodstained knife (Chhurri) P4 taken into possession vide recovery memo Ex.PK by Azhar Iqbal, appellant No.2, is concerned; it was shown as bloodstained, the same was sent for forensic analysis and the swab taken from the blade of the said Chhurri, was declared as human blood vide report (Ex.PAB). On perusal of recovery memo (Ex.PK), it is found that Chhurri was allegedly got recovered by appellant Azhar Iqbal from a room of tubewell of one Saif Ullah Ghabisar, which was concealed inside an ‘iron guarders’ of the roof on 05.06.2022, meaning thereby that this weapon of offence was got recovered after about two months and eleven days, so there is every chance that the blood on the said weapon may have been disintegrated, so in that eventuality, availability of blood on it was not possible after lapse of this period. According to the medical jurisprudence the availability of human blood on the weapon of offence with the afflux of such period is not possible as normally, it disintegrates within a period of three to four weeks. Reliance in this regard is placed upon the judgment passed by the august Supreme Court of Pakistan in case of “MUHAMMAD JAMIL” . So, the recovery of weapon of offence (bloodstained Chhurri) and its positive report by the Punjab Forensic Science Agency (PFSA) are rendered as inconsequential, hence, this piece of evidence too does not provide any MUHAMMAD JAMIL V. MUHAMMAD AKRAM and others (2009 SCMR 120) Crl. Appeal No.28034-J of 2025 11 corroboration to the ocular account. Even otherwise, it is settled by now that evidence of recovery of weapon of offence is corroboratory in nature and it has no intrinsic worth of its own and when the substantive piece of evidence has already been disbelieved or doubted by this Court, no conviction can be based solely on the basis of recovery of weapon of offence, allegedly affected by the police during the course of investigation. Reliance is placed on case of “MUHAMMAD NAWAZ and others”

. Furthermore, the availability of human blood was found on its blade without its blood grouping or DNA, so viewing the facts of the case in its entirety, no judicial certainty and circumstantial guarantee could be attached on the circumstantial evidence adduced and relied by the prosecution.

10. The epitome of above discussion is that since there being no satisfactory basis to uphold the convictions and sentences of the appellants, this appeal is allowed and convictions and sentences awarded to the appellants, namely, Younas Waqar and Azhar Iqbal, through the impugned judgment by the learned trial Court, are hereby set aside, and they are acquitted of the charge. The appellants are in jail, they be released forthwith, if, not required to be detained in any other case. (MUHAMMAD WAHEED KHAN)
JUDGE Approved for Reporting (MUHAMMAD WAHEED KHAN)
